slides.texte_overlay:
5 small posture habits that
give away your nerves
Habit 1: crossing your legs tightly. Wrapping one leg around the other makes your whole body look tense. Sit with both feet on the floor or cross loosely.
Habit 2: hugging your bag. Holding your backpack or laptop against your chest is a shield. Put it down or hang it on your shoulder and let your arms relax.
Habit 3: playing with your rings, watch or sleeves. Small repeated movements pull eyes to your hands. Rest them on the table and leave the accessories alone.
Habit 4: nodding too fast. Constant quick nods look like you're trying to please. Slow, occasional nods look thoughtful, calm and much more confident.
Before: nervous in every meeting. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and a steadier mind that keeps my body calm when the pressure is on.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: nervous in every meeting. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. A steadier mind keeps my body calm under pressure.

slides.texte_overlay: Habit 5: standing with your weight on your toes. It looks like you're ready to run. Settle back onto your heels and feel the floor under your whole foot.
The fix: notice one habit a day. Catch it, correct it, smile. After two weeks, your body learns the calm version and nerves stop showing on the outside.
